explain.say: Window glass is mostly sand, which is silica, mixed with soda ash to lower its melting point and limestone to make it hard-wearing. Crushed recycled glass, called cullet, helps it melt more easily.

explain.say: The mix melts in a huge furnace at around 1,500 degrees Celsius into a thick, glowing liquid. When it cools, its atoms stay jumbled with no crystals, which is why light passes straight through.

explain.say: The molten glass pours onto a long bath of liquid tin. Glass is lighter, so it floats and spreads into a perfectly flat, smooth ribbon, with both faces shiny and no polishing needed.

explain.say: The ribbon is then cooled slowly in a long oven called a lehr. Cooling slowly, called annealing, stops stresses being locked in, so the glass can be cut cleanly without shattering.

faq.a: Ordinary glass is about 70 percent silica sand, plus soda ash, which lowers the melting temperature, and limestone, which makes it resist water. Recycled glass is added too.
asks: What are the ingredients of glass?

faq.a: Glass cools from a liquid without forming crystals, so it has no grain boundaries to scatter light, and its electrons do not absorb visible light. Light passes straight through.
asks: Is glass a liquid or a solid?

faq.q: Why is glass floated on molten tin?
faq.a: Molten tin is perfectly flat, denser than glass and does not mix with it. Glass floating on it spreads into an even sheet with smooth, parallel faces, far better than older methods of rolling or grinding.
asks: What is the float glass process?

faq.a: Annealing means cooling glass slowly and evenly. If it cooled quickly, the outside would harden first and lock in stresses that could make it crack suddenly, especially when cut.
A hard wheel scores a fine line across the surface, then the glass is bent gently along the line and snaps cleanly. Toughened glass cannot be cut afterwards, so it is cut to size first.

facts: The float glass process was developed by Alastair Pilkington and Kenneth Bickerstaff and announced in 1959.
A float glass furnace typically runs continuously for 15 years or more.

quiz.why: The molten glass floats on liquid tin, which is perfectly level, so both faces come out flat and smooth.
